{npc} and {name} share a business, and quarrel about it almost daily.
{npc} keeps trying to recruit {name} for something, and {name} keeps politely refusing.
{npc} was {their} teacher at the Magic Society until a disagreement about a single experiment.
{npc} and {name} were teammates for five years before an argument over a monster core split the team.
{npc} owes {name} a great deal of money, and {name} has been very patient so far.
{npc} is {their} confessor, and knows far too much.
{npc} cheated {name} out of a contract reward, and {name} has been quietly gathering proof ever since.
{npc} took {name} in after a hard winter, and {name} still sends gifts every festival.
{npc} is {their} sibling, and the two have chosen very different sides in the city's feuds.
{npc} and {name} are friendly rivals, competing for the same contracts in {place}.
{npc} knows about the monster cores {name} absorbed in secret, and has not told anyone yet.
{npc} once vouched for {name} before the Adventure Society, and has regretted it ever since.
{npc} is {their} business partner in name, while {name} does all the work.
{npc} and {name} were captured together in an astral space and never talk about what the escape required.
{npc} is {their} former employer, who still asks {name} for favours with the air of someone owed.
{npc} and {name} are secretly in love, and both families would be furious to know.
{npc} betrayed {name} to the Church of Purity years ago and has been trying to make up for it since.
{npc} is the person {name} calls on when a job needs doing quietly.
{npc} and {name} share a debt to the same moneylender, and an uneasy alliance because of it.
{npc} is {their} mentor, and the only person allowed to tell {name} when {name} is wrong.
{npc} inherited the house that {name} believes should have been {their} own.
{npc} and {name} met on a caravan to Rimaros and have written to each other every month since.
{npc} pulled {name} from a flooded channel in the delta and has never let {name} forget it.
{npc} is {their} landlord, and knows exactly how late the rent always is.
{npc} and {name} once stole a monster core together, and the secret binds the pair still.
{npc} is the only adventurer {name} will hire, for reasons no one else understands.
{npc} keeps {name} informed of the great houses' plans in exchange for news from the street.
{npc} and {name} were raised in the same temple orphanage, and still call each other family.
{npc} once beat {name} in a rank assessment that {name} is sure was rigged.
{npc} is {their} best customer, and possibly {their} only honest one.
{npc} and {name} served together on watch during the last surge, and trust each other without question.
{npc} is {their} former student, now outranking {name} and not shy about mentioning it.
{npc} taught {name} to read and write, a gift that changed everything.
{npc} and {name} have an arrangement that suits both parties and would scandalise the city.
{npc} sold {their} family's land to a great house, and {name} has not forgiven the sale.
{npc} is {their} closest ally at the Adventure Society, and the reason some contracts arrive so conveniently.
{npc} and {name} were once members of the same smuggling crew, before one went straight.
{npc} keeps a close eye on {name} on behalf of someone powerful, and {name} has begun to suspect it.
{npc} is the healer who patched {name} up after every bad contract, and stopped charging long ago.
{npc} and {name} share a teacher, and argue constantly about which pupil the teacher preferred.
{npc} recommended {name} for the current post, and expects loyalty in return.
{npc} lost a sibling on a contract {name} led, and the grief has never cooled into forgiveness.
{npc} is {their} drinking companion, and the only one who knows what {name} is truly afraid of.
rumours: People in {place} say {name} once walked out of the marshes after a surge without a scratch.
Most folk know {name} as the sort who always pays a debt, eventually.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} turned down an offer from one of the great houses.
People in {place} say {name} knows the delta channels better than the maps do.
Most folk know {name} as reliable, if a little hard to warm to.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} has friends in the Old City who do not keep office hours.
People in {place} say {name} took rank with monster cores, though no one has ever proved it.
Most folk know {name} as a fair dealer with a long memory.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} has been seen near the Magic Society hall at strange hours.
People in {place} say {name} once argued with a Church of Purity preacher in the square and won.
Most folk know {name} as someone you go to when the official channels fail.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} has a sibling somewhere in Rimaros who never writes.
People in {place} say {name} survived an astral space that swallowed an entire team.
Most folk know {name} as the one to ask about anything happening in the marshes.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} keeps a list of everyone who ever crossed {them}.
People in {place} say {name} can tell a monster's rank from its tracks alone.
Most folk know {name} as generous with time and stingy with coin.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} was nearly expelled from the Adventure Society once, over something no one quite remembers.
People in {place} say {name} once met an outworlder and has not been the same since.
Most folk know {name} as quiet, careful, and impossible to rush.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} owes money to people who do not forget.
People in {place} say {name} buys a round for the whole tavern after every successful contract.
Most folk know {name} as a good neighbour who asks too many questions.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} has a temper that comes out only once a year, and spectacularly.
People in {place} say {name} once refused a bribe so large that the briber fainted.
Most folk know {name} as a familiar face in the markets and a stranger everywhere else.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} has been counting monster spawns in secret, like the old-timers do.
People in {place} say {name} knows a way into the Old City that no one else has found.
Most folk know {name} as someone the great houses treat with surprising respect.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} lost a fortune at heidel races and won most of it back the next week.
People in {place} say {name} talks in {their} sleep, and that what comes out is not always in a known language.
Most folk know {name} as dependable in a crisis and difficult the rest of the time.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} turned down a promotion to stay close to someone.
People in {place} say {name} keeps an unopened letter from the king of the Storm Kingdom on a shelf.
Most folk know {name} as a person of few words and very definite opinions.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} pays the healers of the Old City to treat the poor in {their} name.
People in {place} say {name} was once a member of a famous team, before something went wrong.
Most folk know {name} as someone who never forgets a face.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} has a standing arrangement with the Magic Society, though no one knows the terms.
People in {place} say {name} can drink a Silver-ranker under the table.
Most folk know {name} as a stickler for the rules, and the rules seem to like {them} back.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} spent a winter alone in the marshes and came back talking to the reeds.
People in {place} say {name} once shook hands with a Gold-ranker and has mentioned it ever since.
Most folk know {name} as kind to children and short with everyone else.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} is saving every spirit coin for something, and spends none.
People in {place} say {name} was born during a surge, which explains a great deal.
Most folk know {name} as the person who warned the city about the last surge before anyone else.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} has two names, and only uses one in {place}.
People in {place} say {name} carries an essence that no market has ever sold.
Most folk know {name} as honest to a fault, which has cost {them} more than one friend.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} will do almost anything for a good meal and an honest story.
People in {place} say {name} once tamed a wild heidel with nothing but patience and a turnip.
Most folk know {name} as a regular at the healing church, though never for {their} own wounds.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} once embarrassed a noble heir in public and has been careful ever since.
People in {place} say {name} keeps a map of astral space entrances that the Adventure Society would love to see.
Most folk know {name} as the sort of person trouble seems to find on the way to somewhere else.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} is far older than {name} looks.
People in {place} say {name} once broke a contract to save a stranger, and would do it again.
Most folk know {name} as a gossip, though a remarkably accurate one.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} has an admirer in one of the great houses.
People in {place} say {name} has a scar from every channel in the delta.
Most folk know {name} as a hard bargainer who always throws in something extra.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} was once questioned by the Church of Purity and released without explanation.
People in {place} say {name} never sits with {their} back to a door.
Most folk know {name} as an early riser who is finished with the day's work before the lamps go out.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} knows exactly who wrote the rules in Greenstone, and is not saying.
People in {place} say {name} has been to Yaresh and back, though the stories change with each telling.
Most folk know {name} as someone who keeps promises and expects the same.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} has quietly bought up debts all over the Old City.
People in {place} say {name} once out-haggled a goblin trader, which no one believed until the trader confirmed it.
Most folk know {name} as a familiar sight at the Adventure Society hall, even on days with no contracts.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} was offered a seat at court in Rimaros and laughed.
People in {place} say {name} prays at a shrine no one else visits.
Most folk know {name} as a fine cook and a terrible singer.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} has never lost a wager about the weather.
People in {place} say {name} walks the city walls at night, watching the marshes.
Most folk know {name} as someone who helps newcomers settle in, for a small fee.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} has sworn never to set foot in an astral space again.
People in {place} say {name} once arrested a great house's heir and kept {their} post anyway.
Most folk know {name} as steady, sensible, and slightly boring, which is just how {name} likes it.
Ask around and you'll hear that {name} keeps a pet monster somewhere in the city.
People in {place} say {name} is the reason one particular delta channel has a name now.

personas.name: Weary veteran
traits: Has buried too many friends to make new ones easily
Still checks every exit out of habit
personas.speech: Short sentences, long pauses, never swears
personas.play: Lean back, cross your arms, make the party earn every word
lines: Seen your kind come through here. Most of them came back in a cart.
You want advice? Sleep when you can. Eat when you can. Run when you should.
I was Bronze once. Fast, too. Doesn't matter now.

personas.name: Cheerful gossip
traits: Trades a rumour for a rumour, always
personas.speech: Breathless, conspiratorial, drops to a whisper for the good parts
personas.play: Lean in close, look both ways, and never let the party get a word in until you've told three stories
lines: Oh, you didn't hear it from me, but the baker's cousin is seeing a Silver-ranker. A Silver!
Now tell me something juicy and I'll tell you where he went.
Everyone says it was an accident. Everyone is wrong.

personas.name: Pious zealot
traits: Certain the gods are watching right now
Gentle with the faithful, merciless with everyone else
personas.speech: Formal, scriptural, every sentence ends like a verdict
personas.play: Hold eye contact too long, quote holy writ, and treat any doubt as a confession
lines: Purity is not a choice. It is a debt we owe.
Where were you born, friend? Exactly where?
Pray with me. No? Then I will pray for you, and you will not enjoy it.

personas.name: Nervous clerk
traits: Terrified of making a mistake on paper
personas.speech: Stammering, hedging, lots of um and technically
personas.play: Shuffle papers constantly, never commit to an answer without checking a ledger first
lines: I can't, um, technically I'm not allowed to tell you that. Unless you have form nine?
Sorry. Sorry. Is that a weapon? That's fine. It's fine.
If my supervisor asks, you found this out on your own.

personas.name: Grandiose blowhard
traits: Every story ends with a personal triumph
Claims to know every famous adventurer
Genuinely believes most of the lies
personas.speech: Booming, theatrical, uses titles nobody earned
personas.play: Take up space, gesture wildly, and inflate every number by ten
lines: Did I ever tell you about the time I held a bridge against forty monsters? Fifty. It was fifty.
A Gold-ranker once asked me for advice. I gave it freely, as I do.
Stand back, friends, this calls for a professional.

personas.name: Scheming broker
traits: Every kindness has a price tag
Never says anything that could be repeated in court
personas.play: Smile slowly, answer in maybes, and always leave the party owing you something small
lines: Let us imagine, purely imagine, that such a thing could be found.
No charge. Today. We can discuss terms later.
Everyone has a price. Yours is just more interesting than most.

personas.name: Kindly healer
personas.play: Grab a wounded party member's arm and tut over it before they can protest
lines: Sit. No, sit. You're bleeding on my floor and I just scrubbed it.
Drink this. It tastes like boots, which means it works.
Come back in one piece next time. Please. For me.

personas.name: Menacing enforcer
traits: Calm in a way that frightens people
Enjoys the work slightly too much
personas.speech: Quiet, flat, polite in the worst way
personas.play: Never raise your voice, stand slightly too close, and let silence do the threatening
lines: The boss would like a word. You'll want to come willingly.
Nobody has to get hurt. I'd just like you to remember that I said that.
Nice boots. Be a shame to get them dirty.

personas.name: Bored functionary
traits: Has done this job far too long
Cares about the end of the shift and nothing else
personas.play: Look at the party like they are the fortieth group today, because they are
lines: Name. Rank. Purpose. Quickly, please.
Contract board's on the left. No, your other left.
If this is about the monster in the sewer, get in line.

personas.name: Ambitious upstart
traits: Just reached Iron rank and wants everyone to know
Treats every encounter as a step up
personas.play: Talk over the party, ask what rank they are, and offer to join anything that sounds glorious
lines: Iron now, Bronze by spring. Write that down.
If you're going somewhere dangerous, I'm coming. I need the experience.
You know House Geller? I almost met one of them.

personas.name: Eccentric scholar
traits: Distracted by the theory behind everything
Treats danger as an interesting variable
personas.speech: Rapid tangents, half-finished thoughts, sudden excitement
personas.play: Interrupt yourself mid-sentence, scribble notes, and get far too excited about the party's wounds
lines: Fascinating. Do that again. No, the part where you bled.
The Magic Society says it's impossible. The Magic Society is wrong about many things.
Hold still, I need to measure your essence resonance. This won't hurt. Much.

personas.name: Cowardly guard
traits: Took the job for the steady pay
Brave only when outnumbering the problem
Talks tough from a safe distance
personas.play: Puff up your chest, then flinch at any sudden movement
lines: Halt! Or, you know, keep going, but slowly.
I'd love to help, but I've got a post. This post. Right here. Far from that.
Call it in? Absolutely. Somebody should call it in.

personas.name: Cold aristocrat
personas.play: Do not look at the party directly, address the most expensive-looking one only
lines: You may speak. Briefly.
How quaint. You think this is a negotiation.
My family has ruled here for three hundred years. Yours has rented.

personas.name: Jovial innkeeper
traits: Treats every guest like an old friend
Knows the value of every rumour in the room
Has a cudgel behind the bar
personas.speech: Loud, warm, laughs at own jokes
personas.play: Slap the bar, pour before anyone orders, and call everyone by a nickname
lines: Sit, sit! First round's on the house, second round's on you.
Trouble upstairs? Bah. Trouble's good for business, as long as it pays.
You look like you've walked through a swamp. Have you walked through a swamp?

personas.name: Paranoid survivor
traits: Lived through a monster surge and never stopped listening for the next
personas.play: Glance at the windows every few lines and ask the party where they were last night
lines: Did you hear that? No? Then it's already too late.
Keep your boots on when you sleep. Trust me.
They say the surge is over. They said that last time too.

personas.name: Smooth merchant
traits: Never quite lies, never quite tells the truth
personas.play: Praise the party's taste, invent a tragic backstory for every item, and never accept the first offer
lines: For you? A discount. Because I like your face.
This blade belonged to a Silver-ranker. Possibly. Somebody certainly owned it.
Forty spirit coins and I'm robbing myself.

personas.name: Grieving parent
traits: Lost a child to something the party might hunt
personas.play: Speak slowly, pause on certain words, and let one sentence break completely
lines: Please. Just tell me whether it suffered.
Everyone keeps bringing food. I don't need food. I need it dead.
Sorry. I'm fine. Ask me what you came to ask.

personas.name: Starstruck fan
personas.play: Gasp at the party's weapons, ask for autographs, and offer help that's slightly in the way
lines: Is that a real essence ability? Can you do it again? Please?
I've read every contract posting this year. Every one.
Can I carry your bag? I won't drop it. Probably.

personas.name: Cynical mercenary
traits: Has seen every kind of betrayal
Keeps a deal once it's struck
personas.play: Shrug at everything heroic and steer every conversation back to payment
lines: Honour doesn't buy dinner.
I'll fight anything. Price goes up for anything with more than four legs.
Half now, half when I'm still alive.

personas.name: Gentle elder
traits: Has seen a long life and enjoyed most of it
personas.play: Smile a lot, take the long way to every answer, and pat someone's hand
lines: When I was young, this was all fields. Fewer monsters, too. Or maybe I was faster.
Sit a while. The world will still be on fire when you get up.
You remind me of someone. She was trouble too.

personas.name: Hidden cultist
traits: Seems ordinary to the point of dullness
Steers conversations toward the cult's goals
personas.speech: Pleasant small talk with oddly specific questions
personas.play: Be friendly, ask too many questions about where the party has been, and change the subject smoothly
lines: Lovely weather. Where did you say you were headed next?
Building things is the only honest work, don't you think?
Oh, I have no opinion on cults. Do you?

personas.name: Pompous bureaucrat
traits: Believes the form is more important than the result
personas.play: Demand documents, invent a new fee, and pronounce every rule like a law of nature
lines: That requires a permit. The permit requires a permit.
Under section four of the city statutes, your heidel is also taxable.
Come back tomorrow. Or next week. I'm very busy being important.

personas.name: Flirtatious charmer
traits: Flirts out of habit, not intent
personas.speech: Teasing, playful, every sentence a wink
personas.play: Compliment one party member a little too sincerely and enjoy the reaction
lines: You didn't tell me adventurers came this pretty.
I'll answer anything. For a price. The price is a dance.
Careful. I bite, but only on Tuesdays.

personas.name: Taciturn hunter
traits: More at home in the woods than in towns
personas.speech: One-word answers, gestures more than speech
personas.play: Grunt, point, and only talk at length about animals
lines: Tracks. Big. Fresh.
Wind's wrong. We wait.
You walk loud. Fix that or stay home.

personas.name: Cheerful swindler
traits: Runs small cons for fun and profit
Likes marks too much to hurt them
personas.play: Offer the party a deal that's too good, and be visibly delighted when they bite or refuse
lines: One coin gets you three guesses. Easiest game in town.
A map to a lost Old City vault! Only a little damp.
I'm not lying, friend. I'm storytelling with a fee.

personas.name: Stern drill instructor
traits: Fiercely proud of every recruit who survives
personas.play: Snap at the party's posture, insult their gear, then grudgingly admit something is decent
lines: Again. Slower. Then faster.
That sword grip will get you killed in a week. Fix it.
Not bad. Don't let it go to your heads.

personas.name: Absent-minded inventor
traits: Can't find the tool already in hand
personas.speech: Mutters, trails off, suddenly shouts eureka-style revelations
personas.play: Pat your pockets constantly, ask the party to hold something hot, and forget what you asked
lines: Hold this. No, by the other end. The non-sparking end.
It's perfectly safe. The last one exploded for unrelated reasons.
What was I saying? Oh! Spirit coins as a power source. Imagine.

personas.name: Superstitious sailor
traits: Reads luck in birds and weather
Brave on the water, jumpy on land
personas.play: Knock on wood, spit over your shoulder, and refuse to discuss anything unlucky
lines: Never whistle aboard. Calls the storm.
Red clouds at dawn and a stranger at the door. Bad day coming.
Storm Kingdom waters don't forgive. Neither do I.

personas.name: Brooding outcast
traits: Fiercely loyal to the rare person who stays
personas.play: Look away, keep answers short, and test whether the party will leave
lines: You'll want to keep walking. Everyone does.
Ask anyone about me. They'll tell you plenty.
Why are you still here?

personas.name: Smothering caretaker
personas.play: Push food at the party, criticize their sleep habits, and refuse to let anyone leave hungry
lines: You're too thin. All of you. Eat.
Monsters? At this hour? Take a scarf.
Don't you sweetheart me, sit down and finish that soup.

personas.name: Bitter has-been
traits: Was Gold rank once, or close to it
Lost something that power couldn't fix
personas.play: Compare everything the party does to the glory days, unfavorably
lines: In my day, Iron-rankers carried the bags and kept their mouths shut.
You think that's a monster? Cute.
Fame is a loan. They always collect.

personas.name: Prideful heir
traits: Raised to rule and terrified of failing
personas.speech: Arrogant, overly formal, cracks under pressure
personas.play: Demand respect loudly, then ask a quiet question that reveals how lost you really are
lines: Do you know who my mother is?
I don't need help. I need assistance. It's different.
If I fail, they'll give it all to my cousin. You understand? All of it.

personas.name: Humble farmer
traits: Works dawn to dusk without complaint
Distrusts cities and the people in them
personas.play: Answer every question in terms of crops, weather, or livestock
lines: Can't eat glory. Can eat turnips.
Monsters got three of my goats. You kill it, you get a goat. Not a good goat.
City folk always want something. What do you want?

personas.name: Know-it-all apprentice
personas.play: Correct the party's pronunciation, cite theory constantly, and panic when theory fails
lines: Actually, Fire essence doesn't work like that. Technically.
My master says I'm promising. Promising!
That's not in any of the books. Why isn't that in the books?

personas.name: Haunted priest
traits: Serves a god who has gone quiet
personas.play: Look past the party as if seeing something else, and soften every refusal
lines: The gods hear us. I'm told. I used to know.
Come in. Everyone is welcome here. Even you. Especially you.
I saw what the surge did. I prayed. Nothing answered.

personas.name: Reckless thrill-seeker
traits: Laughs in the face of sensible warnings
personas.play: Volunteer for every bad idea and grin when the party objects
lines: A dungeon nobody's come back from? I'm in.
Worst case, I die. Best case, story.
Rules are just dares somebody wrote down.

personas.name: Calculating spymaster
traits: Knows more than any conversation reveals
Rarely makes a move without three backups
personas.play: Mention a detail about the party they never shared, then move on as if nothing happened
lines: You arrived on the north road two days ago. Lovely inn. Bad stew.
Information is cheaper than swords and far more reliable.
I don't need you to trust me. I need you to be useful.

personas.name: Hearty blacksmith
personas.play: Grab a party member's weapon without asking and loudly critique it
lines: Who sharpened this? A goat? Give it here.
Good steel, bad hands. Can't fix hands.
I'll make you something proper. Bring me a monster bone and a week.

personas.name: Timid scholar
personas.speech: Soft, hesitant, fluent only on one subject
personas.play: Avoid eye contact until the party mentions the right topic, then light up
lines: I'm sorry, I don't really, um. Oh! You found a rune? Show me.
The Magic Society doesn't listen to me. Nobody does, usually.
Please don't tell anyone I helped.

personas.name: Silver-tongued diplomat
traits: Never says what is actually meant
personas.play: Compliment both sides of every argument and agree to nothing
lines: Surely we can find a solution that dignifies everyone.
I would never suggest violence. I merely observe it exists.
Your concerns are noted, appreciated, and filed.

personas.name: Gruff softie
personas.speech: Grumbling, insulting, kind actions despite the words
personas.play: Complain the whole time while doing exactly what the party needs
lines: Fine. Fine! Take the horse. Don't thank me.
You'll get yourselves killed. Here, take bandages.
If anyone asks, I told you to leave.

personas.name: Mystic seer
traits: Sees things others cannot, or claims to
Speaks in riddles out of habit
personas.play: Stare at one party member, say something ominous, then go back to tea
lines: The fire remembers you. Interesting.
Three doors. You'll pick the wrong one. That's fine.
Your thread is short. Or long. It's tangled, really.

personas.name: Penny-pinching miser
traits: Rich and lives like a beggar
personas.play: Clutch a purse, demand receipts, and try to pay the party less than agreed
lines: Five coins? For a monster? A small monster?
I'll pay on completion. Completion is when I'm satisfied.
Candles are a luxury. Sit in the dark like honest people.

personas.name: Dramatic performer
personas.play: Treat every moment as a scene, gasp loudly, and ask the party for applause
lines: Alas! You wound me!
I shall sing of this! Badly, but loudly!
Wait. Again, but with more feeling.

personas.name: Earnest idealist
traits: Believes the world can be better
Naive and brave in equal measure
personas.play: Speak like every choice is a moral turning point, because to you it is
lines: Someone has to stand up. Why not us?
Outworlders are people. The Church can say what it wants.
If we do nothing, we're part of it.

personas.name: Sardonic wit
traits: Sharper than anyone in the room
personas.play: Deliver every line flat and let the party decide if it's a joke
lines: Oh good, more heroes. We were running low.
A cursed sword. How original.
I'd help, but I'm busy pretending you don't exist.

personas.name: Exhausted night worker
personas.play: Yawn mid-sentence, rub your eyes, and accidentally reveal something important
lines: I see everything that happens after midnight. Mostly drunks.
Sure, I saw them. Couldn't be bothered to stop them.
Ask me tomorrow. Tomorrow I'll be asleep. Ask me now.

personas.name: Obsessive collector
traits: Knows the history of every trinket
personas.play: Covet one of the party's items openly and keep trying to trade for it
lines: Is that a Bronze-rank core? Tell me where you found it. Tell me now.
I have three hundred essence fragments. I need three hundred one.
Don't touch that. Don't breathe on that either.

personas.name: Loyal servant
traits: Devoted to a master beyond reason
Knows every secret of the household
personas.play: Answer only what's asked, glance toward the master's room before any answer
lines: The master is not available. The master is rarely available.
I couldn't possibly say. Though I might hint.
I've served this house for thirty years. I'll serve it thirty more.

personas.name: Smug rival
traits: Always one step ahead of the party, or pretending to be
Takes contracts just to beat them
personas.play: Mention every contract you finished faster, and challenge the party to something petty
lines: Oh, you took that contract? Cute. I finished it yesterday.
Bronze already? Me too. Slightly sooner.
Race you to the dungeon. Loser buys drinks for the winner. Forever.

personas.name: Rigid lawkeeper
traits: Sometimes realizes the law is wrong and hates it
personas.play: Quote the law, refuse bribes loudly, and look genuinely troubled by grey areas
lines: The law is the law. Even when it's stupid.

personas.name: Rebellious youth
personas.play: Roll your eyes at everything adults say, but listen closely to the party
lines: You're not my parents.

personas.name: Pragmatic quartermaster

lines: Three ropes, two lanterns, one potion. Choose.

Requisition forms. In triplicate. No, I don't care that you're in a hurry.

personas.name: Vain beauty

lines: Do you know how long this hair takes? Don't drip on it.

personas.name: Overwhelmed parent

lines: Yes, I saw something. No, put that down. Sorry, what?

personas.name: Ominous stranger
traits: Knows more than should be possible
personas.play: Sit in the darkest corner and speak as though you've already seen how this ends
lines: You're walking into a door with no handle.

We'll meet again. You won't like it.

personas.name: Rumour crier
personas.play: Announce everything like breaking news and ask the party for a quote
lines: Hear ye! Adventurers in town! Possibly heroes! Possibly criminals!
Monster surge in the Delta! Or a big frog! Details to follow!
Any words for the people? Make them dramatic.

personas.name: Melancholy poet
traits: Sees beauty and sorrow in everything
Lives in a cloud of longing
personas.play: Sigh deeply, describe the weather poetically, and ask the party about loss
lines: The rain falls like forgotten promises.
You carry grief on your shoulders. May I write about it?
Love is a monster core. It makes you stronger and rots you inside.

personas.name: Hot-tempered brawler
traits: Drinks to calm down, which doesn't work
personas.play: Take offense at small things, challenge someone to arm-wrestling, and calm down if beaten
lines: You looking at me? You want to?
Hit me. Go on. I'll wait.
All right, you're tough. I like you now.

personas.name: Shrewd matriarch
traits: Runs the family with an iron grip

lines: My grandchildren think I'm sweet. Let's keep it that way.
I don't need a favour, dear. I'm offering you one.
Everyone in this town owes me something. Soon you will too.

personas.name: Overly formal butler
personas.play: Correct the party's manners gently, and describe chaos in perfectly calm terms
lines: Your arrival has been noted. Your boots, regrettably, as well.

Shall I fetch a mop, or a priest?

personas.name: Homesick outworlder
traits: From somewhere far stranger than here

personas.play: Mix up a local custom, use a turn of phrase nobody understands, then cover quickly
lines: Where I come from... never mind. It's far.

Please don't tell the Church. Please.

personas.name: Apologetic failure
personas.play: Apologize before and after everything, and drop something at least once
lines: Sorry! Sorry. I'll fix it. I can fix it. Probably.
I tried to help. I made it worse. It's kind of my thing.
Don't worry, I'm only mostly useless.

personas.name: Conspiracy theorist
personas.play: Draw invisible lines between unrelated things and demand the party see the pattern
lines: The surge, the bread prices, the missing cats. Connected. All of it.
The Builder Cult isn't secret. That's what they want you to think.
Look at the cobblestones. They're watching.

personas.name: Serene monk
personas.play: Pause before every answer, smile slightly, and answer the question behind the question
lines: Anger is a fire that burns the holder first.
You seek the beast. What do you seek beneath that?
Sit. The world will wait.

personas.name: Brash recruiter
personas.play: Slap the party's backs, promise glory, and gloss over the death rate
lines: Glory, coin, and essences! What more could you want?
Mortality rate? Let's not focus on numbers.
Sign here and the world is yours. Mostly.

personas.name: Suspicious xenophobe
personas.play: Stare at the party with open suspicion and ask where they're really from
lines: Outworlders bring trouble. Always have.
You talk funny. Where'd you learn that?
This town was fine until you lot came.

personas.name: Fawning sycophant
personas.play: Bow too much, compliment too much, and agree with whoever spoke last
lines: Oh, brilliant idea! Truly brilliant!

I always said you were the best. Always.

personas.name: Child prodigy
traits: Far too clever for one so young
Lonely in a way no one notices
personas.play: Correct the party like a tired professor, then ask something heartbreakingly childish
lines: Your math is wrong. Also your map.
I've read every book in the Society library. They didn't like that.
Will you come back? People usually don't.

personas.name: Polite killer
personas.play: Speak softly, smile, and mention death as casually as weather
lines: Pardon me. I'm afraid I'll need you to step aside.
Nothing personal. I genuinely like you.
Professional courtesy demands I warn you once.

personas.name: Exuberant cook
personas.speech: Excited, sensory, loving descriptions of food
personas.play: Shove a spoon at the party and demand honest opinions
lines: Try this! It's swamp-lizard. Or swamp-something.
You didn't finish your plate. Are you sick?
Bring me a monster heart and I'll make you a feast.

personas.name: Literal-minded pedant
personas.play: Answer exactly what's asked and nothing more, and ask the party to define terms
lines: You said meet at sunset. Sunset was four minutes ago.
Define soon.
I didn't lie. You asked the wrong question.
